verdict.rationale: Gazebo's own docs and repo cover every part of the story. Physics runs through Gazebo Physics, with plugin access to ODE, Bullet and DART. Sensor models cover lidar, cameras, IMU, GPS, force-torque and contact sensors, with optional noise. Robot and environment models are available through Gazebo Fuel, and OGRE v2 provides realistic rendering. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of physics and sensor fidelity versus real hardware.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can simulate my robot and its environment with realistic physics and sensor models before touching hardware

citations.quote: Dynamics simulation: Access multiple high-performance physics engines through Gazebo Physics.
A plugin based interface to physics engines, such as ODE, Bullet, and DART.
Generate sensor data, optionally with noise, from laser range finders, 2D/3D cameras, Kinect style sensors, contact sensors, force-torque, IMU, GPS, and more
Access numerous robots including PR2, Pioneer2 DX, iRobot Create, and TurtleBot, and construct environments using other physically accurate models available through Gazebo Fuel.
it's possible to use rendering engines such as OGRE v2 for realistic rendering of environments with high-quality lighting, shadows, and textures.
